header.eyebrow: Stem Bench · pre-registered · corrected 2026-10-24 · studies 1 to 35
header.lede: The models read; they do not hear. Every hearing job Stem Shovel gave a model went to code or data, and the one place a model now improves the audio pipeline is a reading job.

intro.heading: Reading Works
intro.html: Shown the notes, the chart or the page, the frontier tier is close to perfect. The shipped chart-draft configuration scores 99.8 percent per bar, and the production model reads engraved notation at 98.8 percent from a clean image and 99.3 percent from a clean PDF. It also ignores wrong hints: zero of 438 copied. Cheaper models do not hold that line, and Study 2 found that a call shape that works for one model can silently break its sibling.

intro.heading: Listening Does Not
intro.html: Given audio alone, the song check found the right tempo 2 times in 12, at full confidence, and echoed whatever numbers rode beside the audio. With the chart beside the mix it was perfect, because the value was the chart, not the hearing. Study 8 recorded the program's first genuine listening result, and it was narrow: models hear texture change, not form.

intro.heading: Code and Data Took the Hearing Jobs
intro.html: The summed tempo detector survived stems engineered to break it, the classical stack held its ground against published neural models, and a tempo ladder retired the octave error class by representation. Study 12 took the last hearing job with no model at all: aligning a rendered chart against the recording placed mid-song section boundaries within about a tenth of a second on a real song.

intro.heading: Real Audio Resets the Ceiling
intro.html: Study 13 measured the chord path on a real recording: 38.2 percent, against 95.8 on the synthetic bench, so every synthetic number in this series is a ceiling, not an estimate. A text-only reconciler pass then fixed twelve bars and broke none, the first time in the series a model improved a hearing result, and it did so by reading the pipeline's outputs rather than listening. Study 17 then ran the rematch: the neural chord reader that lost the synthetic gate reads the same recording at 77.6 percent, past the reconciled ceiling, and the reconciler broke sixteen bars the moment the draft no longer came from the notes it reads. Study 18 validated two matcher fixes the app found in the bench's own fixture: the shipped floor moved from 38.2 to 53.9 percent, worth as much as the reconciler pass, with the ceiling unchanged. Study 19 then gated the app's TypeScript port of the winning chord reader at perfect parity, zero disagreeing frames in 7,102, so the real-audio numbers now describe the shipped feature itself. Studies 20 and 20b are the program's first full refutations, published as found: the note channel cannot dress the model's chords in the chart's colors, and the one rule that survived split 81 percent against zero on held-out songs, its precision a function of arrangement density rather than a number a card could print. Study 21 then graded the shipped reader on those same held-out songs: its roots generalize at 90 percent across the whole charted catalog, and the one gate it fails is the grade's own vocabulary. Studies 22 and 23 then ran the recording-to-chart question end to end: the bar grid cannot yet be derived (or even certified, the program's truth being coarser than the question), and the production draft composition fails every gate on the chart the app would parse while its JSON channel quietly holds the best chord numbers the program has measured, so the named fix is deterministic rendering, not better ears. Study 23b then removed the training wheels and collapsed the draft on every song, and its same-day correction is the arc's real lesson: the recordings are metronome-exact at their declared tempos, the collapse came from the bench's own alignment ruler (whose 'first bar' sat four bars late on two songs, so the simulated tap was never a tap), one chart seemed 13 bars longer than its recording plays (a second correction traced that to the bench's own chart fixture), and with the true grid the shipped reader's inputs are already near chart-grade on the arrangement-matched songs, and Study 25 then measured the draft end to end on that grid: exact parity on letter-lands, above baseline on peaceful-dreams, with sub-bar anchor phase left as the named open problem once the second correction resolved the apparent mismatch into a bench fixture error.

provenance: {{stemBench.studiesSpelled|cap}} pre-registered studies, October and November 2026: {{stemBench.scoredRunsDisplay}} scored cells across {{stemBench.modelsSpelled}} gateway models at temperature 0. Each study is registered by commit before its first scored run and published as found; the full catalog lives in the study index below, one page per study. Most ground truth is built by construction (hand-authored progressions, MusicXML scores, synthesized mixes), and the later studies add real recordings scored against the band's own declarations. Production prompts and call shapes are ported verbatim, and grading is mechanical. Three neural MIR baselines and the zero-spend DSP instruments are not counted in the model census. Every amendment and correction, including the dated correction to Study 3, is disclosed and committed.
footer: Pre-registered briefs, the corpus, the synthesis and grading code, and all analyses live in the stem-bench repository (BRIEF.md, REPORT.md). The product under test is Stem Shovel, Lightning Jar's music collaboration app. Sibling programs: AEO Bench and Barkup Bench.
